name: Native American Proverbs
era: Indigenous Oral Traditions of the Americas
summary: Sacred oral reflections on deep kinship with the living earth, seven-generation foresight, and walking in balance.
bio: Across hundreds of sovereign nations—from the Lakota, Hopi, and Haudenosaunee to the Cherokee and Navajo—Native American oral wisdom teaches that humanity is not separate from nature, but an intimate thread in the sacred tapestry of creation. Preserved through elders, oral narratives, and ceremonial songs, these reflections emphasize deep listening, humility, and moral responsibility toward unborn generations.

keyWorks.title: Great Law of Peace (Haudenosaunee)
keyWorks.description: Foundational democratic and ethical principles anchored in peace, reason, and foresight.

keyWorks.title: Oral Teachings of the Elders
keyWorks.description: Centuries of oral transmission honoring the Four Directions and the cycle of seasons.

keyWorks.title: Sacred Earth Speeches & Songs
keyWorks.description: Recorded reflections from leaders like Chief Seattle, Sitting Bull, and Black Elk.

pillars.description: The sacred truth that all living beings, waters, skies, and creatures are our relatives.
In every decision, we must consider the impact on our descendants seven generations ahead.
Taking only what is needed, giving thanks, and leaving no scars on the sacred soil.
Honoring the silent, omnipresent sacred presence in wind, stone, and breath.

whyTimeless: Indigenous reflections call modern civilization back to sanity, reminding us that we did not weave the web of life; we are merely a strand in it.
